name: Mog battle

card.summary: A mog battle is a forum thread where users post two faces and members vote on which one 'mogs' the other, giving participants a direct comparison of their looks.
card.note: Public face comparisons can be harsh for participants.

quick.overview:
In looksmaxxing slang, to 'mog' someone is to outclass them in appearance. A mog battle is a thread that puts two photos side by side, from friends, rivals or the poster himself, and asks the community who wins.

Threads on looksmax.org carry titles like 'mog battle between my friends' or 'mog battle who mogs', and replies are short verdicts, sometimes with feature-level commentary.
quick.how: A poster uploads two photos and asks 'who mogs'. Respondents answer with a pick and often cite features such as facial structure.
quick.risks: The format invites blunt, sometimes insulting responses. Opinions vary between voters and depend on photo quality and angle.

lead: A mog battle is a comparison thread on looksmax.org in which a poster shows two people's photos and the community votes on which one 'mogs' (outclasses) the other [1][2][3].

Threads range from friends and forum members to subscription-service matchups, and carry titles such as 'mog battle who mogs' and 'mog battle me vs...' [4][5]. Replies usually name a winner and sometimes comment on specific features, for example a poster pointing to the sphenoid area as the reason one face looked a certain way [3].
For users, the threads give a quick read on how a face compares and which features stand out.

chain: Community votes and names standout features
angle.text: Mog battles give users comparative feedback on faces and features. They do not change appearance themselves, but participants can use the comments to decide what to work on.

paras: The format asks voters to pick the better-looking of two people. Replies are brief and informal, for example a one-line choice of 'the second one' [2], and some focus on bone structure features [3].

Mog battles are one of several comparison and rating formats on the forum, alongside appearance-rating threads. Many thread titles (for example those pairing a user with another member or a named rival) show the format used for social competition as well as feedback [5][6].
